headline: How steroids
body: They trigger apoptosis. Programmed cell death, switched on deliberately by the cell.
punch: And the switch is the androgen receptor itself.

headline: The experiment
body: Cortical neurons grown from rat brain, then dosed with different androgens for 24 hours or 3 days. They measured mitochondrial activity, membrane damage via LDH release, and caspase 3/7, which is the enzyme that executes apoptosis.
punch: Three separate readouts of cell death, not one.

headline: Testosterone, nandrolone
body: All three killed neurons by apoptosis. All three raised LDH release, meaning the cell membranes were breaking down. Caspase 3/7 activity went up, confirming the death was programmed rather than accidental.
punch: Same route for all three. Different potencies.

headline: Stanozolol
body: Winstrol produced necrosis instead of apoptosis, and did not raise LDH the way the others did. Necrosis is uncontrolled cell rupture, which triggers inflammation in surrounding tissue.
punch: Not safer. A different death, with an inflammatory tail.

headline: Trenbolone
body: It reduced neurite outgrowth, meaning neurons couldn't extend the connections they use to wire to each other. It also downregulated Tubb3, the gene for beta 3 tubulin, which is the structural protein neurons build those extensions from.
punch: It doesn't just kill cells. It stops survivors connecting.

headline: Nandrolone
body: Nandrolone alone showed reduced mitochondrial activity by 24 hours. Mitochondrial failure comes before the apoptosis signal, so this is an early upstream hit rather than a late consequence.
punch: Deca gets in earlier in the death pathway.

headline: The mechanism
body: Flutamide, an androgen receptor blocker, almost completely prevented the toxicity. Mitochondrial function held, membranes stayed intact, apoptosis was inhibited.
punch: Block the receptor and the neurons live.

headline: Which is the problem
body: The receptor causing the neuronal death is the same receptor producing the anabolic effect. There is no version where you block one and keep the other. Antioxidants and diet have not been tested against this and there is no evidence they help here.
punch: This is on target damage, not a side effect you can supplement around.

headline: What you can actually do
body: Toxicity in these studies was dose dependent and worsened with repeated exposure versus single dose. Compound choice matters too, since trenbolone hit neurite outgrowth and gene expression while others did not.
punch: Dose, duration and compound are the only levers here. There is no fourth one.
